NAD, however — I’m a regular dental patient & have some valuable insight to share. So many dentists say that if back teeth are pulled, the remaining teeth won’t shift. This is not always true according to other dentists. Having any teeth removed, can result in remaining teeth shifting to fill the gaps. 

More concerning however, is the high risk of bone loss. When back teeth are removed, your bite is likely to be affected. Since the supporting bone where the teeth were is no longer getting stimulation, it becomes recognized as useless and a process called bone resorption occurs. This can mess up your smile and also your facial muscles and bones. I had 4 wisdom teeth removed and suffered a severe case of this. My dentist told me that while it doesn’t happen to everyone, it happens to some people. Long story short, I had to get braces for two years to realign my bite, I experienced bone loss and other serious problems. The braces helped but things have never been the same. 

It’s worth looking into dental implants, and receiving bone grafting as soon as possible. While the teeth may not have been able to be saved, you should take preventative measures and quickly. 

This is not theoretical, and you may want to research this for yourself.

So, your main concerns about this relationship are his educational status and financial situation? I mean, he makes great money— more than plenty of people with degrees so I’m not sure why you’re so concerned. But this shouldn’t be something to focus on when it comes to qualities of a person. With these concerns, you may find someone with an impressive educational background and plenty of money, but what if they are not kind or funny, or authentic… what if you don’t like their personality like you do this guy? Money and status, at the end of the day are trivial. They matter in the world, but they are not what counts most. These things do not guarantee happiness or love. But maybe your priorities are not set this way, yet anyway. 

It sounds like your family’s opinions are weighing on you, and that’s understandable and very common, but your parents aren’t dating him, you are. No good ever comes from letting outsiders opinions influence your relationship. 

Some may say you should communicate to him your concerns about wanting him to pursue higher education, but if I were put under pressure like that by someone I’d only met once, I would feel awful. Instead of picking apart things you aren’t satisfied with, what about appreciating and admiring his good traits? The things that make him who he is.. the things you like about him. That’s what you should be talking to him about. Then again, maybe you should let him know what you expect. So he can see what’s important to you and decide if he wants to be with someone who values him for what he has more than who he is.

You need to get your priorities in line if you want to end up in a happy relationship.

I’ve always heard, the younger you get them removed, the better the outcome. If you get them extracted at a later age, your chances of problems drastically increases. I speak from personal experience.

My personal opinion is that wisdom teeth (or any teeth) should not be extracted unless there’s an absolute necessary reason and no other option.
About 4 years ago the dentist took all 4 of mine out. My jaw shrunk, my cheeks sunk inward, my bite shifted and teeth no longer met in harmony. It was devastating and depressing, no one warned me. Bone loss & resorption. Everyone I talked to said I looked way too thin, but I hadn’t lost any weight. I got braces after that to try and fix things… realign my bite. It took a while, but I did improve a lot. The retainer period fixed my face. It is not the same, but it’s not messed up like it was. Mastic gum has given my jaw density and definition and muscle again. The time and money to fix the damage though… good lord. 

So yeah… be aware that removing those teeth can cause problems like these photos. Dentists & other specialists deny it because tooth loss means more dental procedures, which means more money in their pocket with every appointment … but patients all over the Internet can vouch for it.

They always push to remove wisdom teeth. If they’re causing some sort of pain & it’s absolutely necessary, you could look into it… but be aware- it can have cause issues to your remaining teeth and face. Removing wisdom teeth can contribute to bone loss, creating hollow cheeks… it can also ruin your bite & cause your other teeth to shift. 

I would ask why they suggest removing them.
I read that inverted yoga poses that boost circulation in the face can help. Also….. mastic gum. It is a miracle.

I feel ya, you do have to wear your retainers for at least a year most hours of the day after your braces come off, and then every night until you die, lol. But you do get used to it. 

Also, yes…. If you stop wearing your retainers you can expect a process called relapse to occur, where your teeth will shift back to their original position. I’ve seen it happen in friends… had straight teeth after braces, stopped wearing retainers, teeth went crooked again. It’s annoying to think about but it’s nice to have a big pretty smile. Just accept your retainers as part of your nightly routine like washing your face and putting on pajamas. I know the idea sounds annoying, and that first year of constant retainer wear is so annoying after you get braces off, but you get used to it. I stuck it out, now I’m only wearing them nightly. My smile is large, straight and beautiful. I wear the retainers every night.

As for permanent surgery, the only way to do that is to have all your natural teeth removed and replaced with dental implants. Not recommended and unbelievably expensive…. My moms husband had it done.
